newsitem.title: GREECE: NAUGHTY GREEK PUBLIC WORKERS TO BE SACKED, MIN.
newsitem.headline: NAUGHTY GREEK PUBLIC WORKERS TO BE SACKED, MIN.

text.p: Greek civil servants who are found to have been involved in misconduct will be sacked, Interior and Public Administration Minister Alekos Papadopoulos said.

"Who says civil servants cannot be sacked? This has become one of the great myths of modern Greece," he was quoted as saying in an interview published on Thursday in the financial weekly 'Ekonomikos Tahydromos'.

He said a radically revised code of conduct for the civil service - due by the end of February - would create "a more flexible, decisive disciplinary code" and put paid to the idea that civil servants cannot be punished.
Greece's public service has long been considered a fiefdom of government and political party interests.
Many state utilities and companies have traditionially had their ranks swollen with unqualified political appointments, making the enterprises economically unsound and ineffective.
As part of efforts to trim the bloated public sector, the government recently announced it would only appoint one new civil servant for every five departures.
Successive governments have made such pledges in recent years but civil service ranks have remained largely unchanged. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
